_doc: JStack systems registry — every system bundled by the JStack plugin (hooks, skills, runtime mechanisms) that must be tracked, documented, and live-testable. A host machine may federate this file into its own systems registry via an `imports:` field and stamps each entry with `origin: "jstack"` + the resolved plugin version at read time. Maintenance rule: every entry lives where its code lives — edit JStack systems in JStack, host systems in the host registry, never both. Every entry MUST declare a `test` so verification is callable on demand from any surface (CLI, dashboard, work-Claude debugging).

_schema.kind: hook | skill | system | subsystem — 'hook' = Claude Code lifecycle hook (PreToolUse, SessionStart, etc.). 'skill' = invocable slash-command skill shipped under skills/. 'system' = composite mechanism (rules-injection pipeline, install flow). 'subsystem' = nested sub-feature inside a parent.
_schema.name: string — display name
_schema.code: array of code paths (relative to plugin root)
_schema.config: array of config paths (relative to plugin root unless ~/-prefixed)
_schema.docs: array of doc paths inside the plugin (typically docs/systems/{id}.md)

test.type: script | endpoint — 'script' = CLI executable, runs in-place, exit 0 = pass. 'endpoint' = HTTP POST handled by a host process (reserved for host-side wrappers).
test.path: string — for type=script, path relative to plugin root. for type=endpoint, URL path.
test.description: string — one-line description of what the test verifies

systems.name: Cross-Tree Rule Injection
systems.description: PreToolUse hook that injects path-matched ~/.claude/rules/*.md bodies into Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit calls — works regardless of session launch CWD, so cross-tree agents pick up the right conventions on every file mutation.

test.description: Live test of the real hook script via its PreToolUse JSON stdin contract: cold-fire (matches rule + emits additionalContext on first call), consecutive-dedup (same session, no transcript growth → no re-inject), threshold re-fire (transcript grown past JSTACK_RULE_REINJECT_BYTES → re-inject). Runs hermetically against a temp fixture via JSTACK_RULES_DIR + JSTACK_CACHE_ROOT overrides — never touches real markers or shipped rules.

systems.notes: Registered in hooks/hooks.json — Claude Code auto-loads when the plugin is installed. Kill switch: JSTACK_PATH_RULES_DISABLED=1. Re-fire threshold: JSTACK_RULE_REINJECT_BYTES (default 400000 ≈ 100K tokens). Defensive: any exception → silent exit 0, never blocks the tool. Marker files live at /tmp/jstack-rule-cache/<session_id>/<rule>.marker storing the transcript byte offset at last injection.

systems.name: SessionStart Timeline Injection
systems.description: SessionStart hook that injects the seat's last N timeline entries (via bin/log_event tail) into every new session as additionalContext — the READ half of the running-memory loop (the WRITE half is the session-end self-write / Stop-hook line). Which seats get injected and how many entries is the timeline_inject map in the review config ({"agent/submode": N, "*/submode": N}); unlisted seats get nothing. Sub-mode resolves from cwd: first segment under {agent_root}/{Name}, else 'chat' (cockpit sessions stay at the agent root, so the project-dir key / memory is never moved); 'review' is skipped.

test.description: Live test of the real hook via its SessionStart JSON stdin contract against a hermetic temp agents tree (JSTACK_REVIEW_CONFIG override): agent-root cwd → 'chat' seat injected; explicit submode cwd → that seat's entries; 'review' submode → no output; non-workspace cwd → no-op; unlisted seat → nothing; interactive_only honored (headless spawn gets nothing, pty session injected); kill switch honored; emitted payload is valid SessionStart hook JSON.

systems.notes: Registered in hooks/hooks.json — auto-loads when the plugin is installed. Kill switch: JSTACK_TIMELINE_INJECT_DISABLED=1 (legacy JSTACK_CONTINUITY_INJECT_DISABLED honored). Reads agent_root + timeline_inject from JSTACK_REVIEW_CONFIG (default ~/.claude/jstack/review.json), same as the engine. Defensive: any error → exit 0, never blocks a session. Sub-mode resolution is kept identical to bin/session-review-spawn resolve_submode and the Stop hook's agent_source — if they drift, a seat reads back entries it never wrote.

systems.name: Install Rules
systems.description: Symlinks (or copies, with --copy) every rule under rules-stage/ into ~/.claude/rules/ so the rule bodies auto-load by glob match on every Claude Code session.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, name matches directory.

systems.notes: Default mode symlinks (auto-track plugin updates); --copy snapshots for offline edit; --force overwrites existing files. Symlinks point into the plugin cache, so a version bump invalidates the link target — re-run with --force after major updates. /jstack:install-rules.

systems.name: Work
systems.description: Gets the agent battle-ready on a topic before doing the work: orient (date + injected seat timeline), resolve project → repo, determine stack, load every relevant skill via the Skill tool, survey recent changes (git log/status + topic file search), read the core files, and report a grounded lay of the land. Preparation only — no code changes, no state writes, no PR.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, name matches directory.

systems.notes: Args: [@project] <topic>. No registry read — leans on the agent's own loaded identity for project + stack. @project resolves a repo name case-insensitively under userConfig.repo_root (default parent of agent_root); unknown → list candidates and stop. No @project → own project; multi-project agent + ambiguous topic → infer from topic, else ask one question. Skill selection matches stack+topic against live skill descriptions (no hardcoded table), loads inclusive. /jstack:work.

systems.name: Handoff
systems.description: Generates a concise session handoff doc and opens a fresh Claude Code terminal preloaded with it via bin/open-terminal-here. Supports @agent targeting: resolves another agent's workspace under user_config.agent_root and boots the new session there — walk-up does the identity switch.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, bin/open-terminal-here adapter is executable.

systems.notes: Args: [@agent] [focus]. @agent resolves {Name} case-insensitively under agent_root; target cwd = chat/ subdir if present else agent root; unknown name → list available agents and stop. Focus narrows scope. Writes handoff-context.md to the TARGET cwd, then open-terminal-here with --append-system-prompt-file. Cross-agent docs are briefings: name who hands off, mark user-locked decisions. Adapter overridable earlier in PATH. /jstack:handoff.

systems.name: Audit
systems.description: Writes a claims document (audit-brief.md: protocol + Original Issue / What Was Done / Claimed Verifications / Caution Flags / Blast Radius / Pitfalls) and opens a fresh terminal via bin/open-terminal-here where a trust-nothing auditor verifies every claim from source and reports CONFIRMED/REFUTED/UNVERIFIABLE. Report-only — the auditor changes nothing.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, bin/open-terminal-here adapter is executable.

systems.notes: Args: [focus] [@agent], order-agnostic. @agent resolves like handoff under agent_root (auditor boots under that agent's identity). Caution Flags section is mandatory — user-stated 'don't break X' constraints verbatim, verified first. Auto-start: kickoff prompt passed as a pre-quoted positional claude arg (adapter flattens args via $*). Auditor asks first only if genuinely blocked, else begins immediately. /jstack:audit.

systems.name: Recall
systems.description: Replays the timeline for a date or period and outlines what happened, scoped to an agent/submode or all seats. Reads through bin/log_event — the store is the only source, never a summary of it.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, bin/log_event adapter is executable.

systems.notes: Args: [yesterday|monday|jan 24|YYYY-MM-DD[..YYYY-MM-DD]] [agent[/submode]|all] [detailed]. Date-or-period questions only — a keyword question ("when did we ship X?") is a log_event grep, not this. /jstack:recall.

systems.name: Tag
systems.description: Files the session under a timeline subject by hand: reads the vocabulary through bin/log_event (with the marker saying what this session already carries), offers the fitting names as a pick, and mints only through the 'Other' branch. The same assignment the session-end self-write makes automatically, available mid-session and correctable.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, bin/log_event adapter is executable.

systems.notes: Args: [tag] to set, -[tag] to detach, --session <id> to retarget; empty offers the vocabulary as a pick. The gates live in the CLI, not here — `tag new` requires a description and `tag set` refuses an unknown name, so the skill can never mint by accident. /jstack:tag.

systems.name: Split Off
systems.description: Dubs the current session into a new terminal via bin/dub-session — a verbatim copy of the conversation under a fresh id, opened in its own window and diverging forward. Where handoff distills to a brief, this keeps the whole transcript.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, bin/dub-session and bin/open-terminal-here adapters are executable.

systems.notes: No args. The copy carries the full transcript, so the fork costs a session's context rather than a summary of it — use when the exploration itself is the thing worth branching. /jstack:splitoff.

systems.name: Print Transcript Path
systems.description: Prints the absolute path of the session's local JSONL transcript file — the answer to "where is this conversation stored on disk".

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists and frontmatter is well-formed.

systems.notes: No args. No adapter — resolves the path from the session's own environment. /jstack:print.

systems.name: Prompt Injection Check (pict)
systems.description: bin/pict renders everything a session spawned from a given directory would actually receive — globals, CLAUDE.md walk-up, auto-memory, timeline injection, anchored path rules, hook injectors — as one ordered markdown document with per-source token weights. The way to see a seat's real context budget instead of reasoning about it.

test.description: Hermetic run against a fixture home tree, fixture rules, fixture review config and a stub log_event — no real ~/.claude or timeline touched.

systems.notes: Answers "what does this seat actually load" from the real injectors rather than from what the mds claim. Resolves symlinks (macOS /var → /private/var) when keying a directory.

systems.name: Timeline Log
systems.description: Timeline sqlite store ({timeline_dir}/timeline.db) written and read by bin/log_event — block format, chronological order, pipeline-task consolidation, direct/indirect origin, and a session→tag relation naming the subject a stretch of work was about. The day's spine: feeds daily briefs, nightly reviews, and seat injection.

test.description: Runs the real bin/log_event against a temp JSTACK_TIMELINE_DIR: block format, detail bullets, chronological insertion, blank-line separation, pipeline-task consolidation (one live block, earliest ts), headline collapse, bad-arg rejection. Tags: the relation migrates onto a pre-tag db, `tag new` needs a description, `tag set` refuses an unknown name instead of minting it, --tag on tail/grep/recall resolves entries through session_id, an undefined tag errors rather than returning silence, and a write with no --session inherits CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID while the explicit flag still wins.

subsystems.name: Stop Timeline Reminder
subsystems.description: Stop hook that blocks an auto session's first stop once, with a log_event reminder, so a cron-spawned run cannot end without writing its timeline entry. A marker makes the second stop pass through, so it reminds rather than loops.

test.description: Pipes fixture Stop-hook JSON through the real hook: auto session blocks once then passes, stop_hook_active honored, user-engaged and tiny transcripts never block, SKIP_SESSION_HOOK=1 never blocks.

subsystems.notes: Only auto sessions are in scope — a typed/TUI transcript is never blocked, since a human ending a session is not a session skipping its record.

systems.notes: Self-contained python3 stdlib — no venv, no host imports. Timeline dir override: JSTACK_TIMELINE_DIR (default ~/Logs/Timeline). Format spec is the rules-stage/timeline.md rule (install via /jstack:install-rules). Hosts with an in-process timeline writer must keep format parity — pin it with a host-side parity test against this bin.

systems.name: Session-End Engine
systems.description: SessionEnd hook → bin/session-review-spawn engine → session_end_action. Default 'selfwrite': resume a disposable DUB of the just-ended session (bin/dub-session) for ONE turn to write its own seat-tagged timeline entry and pick the session's subject tag from the shared vocabulary, then delete the dub — the primary transcript never grows a self-write turn (clean future resume, clean picker; stale dubs pid-swept every engine run). A resumed session that ends again gets the engine-computed last-reviewed boundary injected, scoping the entry to the delta since the resume point. Legacy 'review': claude --print from {agent_root}/{Name}/review/ running the review skill → output parser-validated → retry → escalate (thread extraction + doc reconciliation). Keeps the timeline truthful after every session.

test.description: Imports the real engine under a hermetic temp config: output validator (good passes; missing section / evidence-free walk / log_event-claimed-but-timeline-didn't-grow reject; 'no user turns' + cron paraphrases accepted; host-extended section lists enforced), agent resolution (umbrella dirs, project_dir_map, $HOME → default_agent, review/-dir reviewable convention), atomic claim dedup (live pid loses, stale pid taken over), SPAWN log-line dashboard contract, and the selfwrite prompt itself (formats with every placeholder, names the seat source, links and tags the ORIGINAL session, reads the tag vocabulary before writing to it, steps numbered once each, host-only stamp step omitted where the tool doesn't exist, resume-delta boundary injected only when there is one).

systems.notes: session_end_action selects the behavior: 'selfwrite' (default) resumes the ended session (bin/log_event on the spawned PATH, selfwrite_model/selfwrite_max_turns/selfwrite_timeout_secs) and re-records the reviewed offset past the appended write so a reopen doesn't re-fire; 'review' runs the fresh review/ session (skill_invocation, required_sections, model, max_turns, timeout_secs, tg_classify_cmd, escalate_cmd); 'off' does nothing. Stack requirements: agent workspaces under agent_root with {Name}/review/ (reviewable convention). Config: JSTACK_REVIEW_CONFIG (default ~/.claude/jstack/review.json) — agent_root, default_agent, project_dir_map, extra_path, log_file, plus the action-specific keys above. Kill switch: JSTACK_REVIEW_DISABLED=1. Loop guard: SKIP_SESSION_HOOK=1 on every spawn. Multi-entry-point safe: per-session atomic claim means a host SessionEnd hook and the plugin hook never double-act.

systems.name: Push
systems.description: Commits and pushes the work touched in the current session to whatever repo(s) those files live in — supports session-scoped (default) or all-pending (`all`) modes, and `0` to commit without pushing.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, name matches directory.

subsystems.name: Session File List
subsystems.description: Prints the paths a session wrote, read from its own transcript — the stage list for /push, so which files are mine is never inferred from a shared working tree.

test.description: Drives the real binary against a fixture HOME, a synthetic transcript and a throwaway repo: the stage list is written-paths intersected with what git still sees a change at, in first-write order, deduped; subagent (sidechain) writes are included and Read/Bash calls are not; unchanged, gitignored and non-repo paths stay out of the stage list while remaining in --all and --json; a tracked file deleted on disk still stages; a torn final transcript line is skipped rather than fatal; a file another session left dirty is structurally unlistable. Every blind case — no session id, no transcript, one id matching two transcripts — exits nonzero instead of returning an empty list.

subsystems.notes: The list comes from the transcript and never from `git status` — that is what stops a dirty shared tree from being a judgment call, and why an agent can stage all of it without deciding anything. Blind spot by design: writes made through Bash (mv, sed -i, a script emitting files) never become tool calls, so /push still adds those by hand. Transcript resolution matches the print skill — id-globbed across project dirs, never newest-by-mtime, which under concurrent sessions hands back another session's file. Also answers for a dead session (--session <id>), which is how orphaned work gets attributed to whoever actually wrote it.

systems.notes: Authorization gate: only runs if the user explicitly said push/commit/ship/land in this session. Resolves repos from the touched-file list (works from a non-repo cockpit). Hard rules: no --no-verify, no --amend, no Co-Authored-By, no `git add -A`, sensitive paths skipped, never force-push main/master. `all` mode groups pending changes into per-unit-of-work commits with a one-line plan up front. /jstack:push.

systems.name: Report
systems.description: Closes out a task: every finding is settled as its own commit or a filed GitHub issue before the report is written, so nothing real leaves the session as prose.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, name matches directory, and the file-issue adapter it calls is present and executable.

subsystems.name: Issue Filing
subsystems.description: Files a GitHub issue for an unfixed finding AND places it on the board its owner reads, resolving repo -> project -> intake column live from GitHub. Exactly one type label (bug / optimization / feature) is required and created on repos that lack it.

test.description: Drives the real binary against a stub gh: a filed issue is added to its board and the intake column set (TODO/Backlog/Triage found by name, never by position); a repo linked to no project still files, one linked to several is skipped rather than guessed unless --project names it; a project marked [not-intake] is excluded so a work board cannot steal filing, though --project still selects it; exactly one type label is required and a missing one is created on the repo, with an uncreatable one filing untyped and saying type=none in its receipt; an unknown non-type label is dropped instead of taking the issue down; and every blind or refusing state - no gh, failed graphql, null repo, issues disabled, no body - exits nonzero so the caller can never report a number it did not get.

subsystems.notes: Board routing is read live from repository.projectsV2 rather than a local repo->board map, because a second copy of a fact GitHub already owns rots silently. Placement is best-effort AFTER creation: an issue that files but fails to board still exits 0 with board=none in its receipt, since losing the issue would be the worse outcome. Portable with no config: a machine whose repos are linked to no project gets plain issues.

systems.notes: Fixed, or filed - the rule the skill enforces. A break in reach gets fixed and becomes its own commit; a break not fixed becomes an issue in the owning repo, with a body a cold reader can act on. Replaces the reporting template that used to live in the host root CLAUDE.md, where findings could be mentioned in prose and lost at session end. Commit mechanics are NOT restated here - the skill hands committing to /jstack:push, which owns the commit contract. /jstack:report.

systems.name: Issue
systems.description: Works one assigned GitHub issue from open to a PR: reads the brief, boards it, builds the fix in a worktree, opens the PR, answers on the issue.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, name matches directory, and the place-issue adapter it calls is present and executable.

subsystems.name: Board Placement
subsystems.description: Puts an existing issue on a work board and sets its status column, resolving board and column live from GitHub by title.

test.description: Drives the real binary against a stub gh: the card is added AND its column set, and a column that could not be set is reported as unset with exit 5 rather than claimed; an exact board title beats a substring that also matches, an ambiguous or unknown title exits 4 without placing, and a closed board is not a placement target; a user-owned account resolves like an org one even though gh exits non-zero on that call; the dry run mutates nothing and exits 5 on a column that does not exist.

subsystems.notes: Companion to file-issue, and a different act: file-issue answers where a NEW finding goes (an intake column, by repo linkage); this answers where work-in-progress is visible (a work board, by title). Adding is idempotent, so a resumed session re-running it does not duplicate its card. Board titles are read live for the same reason file-issue reads linkage live - a local board->id table is a second copy of a fact GitHub owns.

systems.name: Show Me
systems.description: Surfaces the result of the current topic in its real viewer instead of describing it. A fidelity-ladder command: mode token raw|live picks source-code vs live-running surface, default prefers an in-code preview. Classifies the artifact (code, preview, image, doc, mockup, data, app, web page, diff) and opens it via bin/open-artifact / Xcode (xed) / sim. Optional focus arg narrows which artifact.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, bin/open-artifact adapter is executable.

systems.notes: Args: [raw|live] [focus]. mode = reserved token on the fidelity ladder: raw -> source code (iOS: xed <View>.swift in Xcode; mockup/doc -> its .html/.svg/.md source not the render); default -> cheapest visual, prefers an in-code preview (SwiftUI #Preview in Xcode canvas, Storybook, Quick Look) over a heavier surface; live -> running env (sim build+launch+screenshot, dev server + live URL) via the project's run/sim/device skill. focus narrows the artifact; omitted shows the most recent salient result. Static artifacts (image/pdf): default==live==open in viewer, raw==source-if-any. Fallbacks: requested surface unavailable -> drop to nearest rung and say so; no visual -> textual render; adapter/xed nonzero -> report absolute path. bin/open-artifact self-detects platform (open / xdg-open|gio / start), overridable earlier in PATH. /jstack:showme.

systems.name: Day Audit
systems.description: Reverifies a whole day's shipped work across every repo, each audited under its OWNING agent for real domain context. Treats that day's timeline (the agents' claims) as a claims document, gathers the day's commits in each repo under repo_root (all refs), resolves each repo to its owning agent via the agent registry, fans out one regression auditor per repo-with-commits told to load that agent's role file + the repo's CLAUDE.md first (focus on bug-fix commits: real fix? regressed another issue? broke a consumer? smuggled in something big?), then synthesizes an IMPROVED/NEUTRAL/REGRESSED verdict per app and flags claim<->commit gaps. Report-only on code; always writes one timeline block recording the verdict.

test.description: Validates SKILL.md exists, frontmatter is well-formed, name matches directory, bin/log_event is executable.

systems.notes: Args: [today|yesterday|<date>], date normalized in python3 (defaults today). Portable repo discovery: repo_root userConfig, else parent of agent_root, scanned for */.git. Ownership: agent_registry userConfig (else {agent_root}/agents.json) — each agent entry's {workspace, repos}; repo<->registry matched by normalized name (case + _/- folded) against BOTH local dir basename and git origin, so WBIS_iOS==WBIS-iOS. Owning-agent context delivered by instructing the auditor to read {workspace}/CLAUDE.md + {repo}/CLAUDE.md first (in-process subagents don't inherit a foreign CLAUDE.md via cwd); unowned repo -> generic auditor, coverage never drops. Per-day commits via `git log --all --no-merges --since/--until --date=local` so develop/feature/pushed work is covered. Verdict logged to the AUDITED day's file: `log_event day-audit --at <now> --date <DAY> --pipeline-task day-audit#<DAY>` — one block per day, replaced on re-run. Report-only on repos (never edits code); high-severity findings re-verified by the parent before repeating. /jstack:day-audit.

systems.name: Scheduler
systems.description: Deterministic daemon that fires one-time and recurring agent runs on RFC-5545 RRULE schedules — the piece that lets JStack START a session, not just review and remember one. Timeout counts from spawn, the daemon owns child pgids, TTFT/stall watchdogs kill hung turns, catch-up covers downtime.

test.description: Runs the real package against a hermetic temp SCHEDULER_HOME: install config drives timezone/spawn env/spawn PATH; workspace resolution (override > resolver hook > registry > agent_root) with seat_rules applied only when the seat is real; a broken resolver spec raises rather than silently relocating every run; permission_mode defaults to bypassPermissions and resolves job>category>default; VTIMEZONE derived for US-DST, last-Sunday and no-DST zones; registry add/list/remove round-trip through the CLI; and a real daemon boot serving /health. Skips with a clear message when the host python lacks python-dateutil. Never touches a real registry, state dir, or running daemon.

systems.notes: One package, every machine — nothing about a host is written into it. A host declares itself in {install}/config/scheduler.json: timezone, spawn_env, spawn_path_prepend, spawn_dirs, workspace_resolver ('module:function') + python_path, agent_root / agent_registry, seat_rules. SCHEDULER_HOME roots config/ and state/ (default: the package's parent); SCHEDULER_CONFIG_DIR / STATE_DIR / CREDENTIALS_DIR / API_PORT / INSTALL_FILE override individually. Requires python-dateutil and the claude CLI. Runs under launchd/systemd as `python3 -m scheduler`; mutations go through `python3 -m scheduler.cli`. permission_mode defaults to bypassPermissions because an unattended run has nobody to answer a prompt — narrowing it per job or per category is deliberate, not a default to reach for. Control API binds 127.0.0.1 only, no auth.

systems.name: Agent Inbox
systems.description: Addressed messaging in two forms — an UPDATE to a seat, delivered once at its next SessionStart; a TASK to a session, which spawns one, ties it to the sender's, and opens a two-way channel enforced at Stop. bin/msg writes a `messages` table alongside the timeline and is its only sanctioned writer.

test.description: Runs the real bin/msg against a temp timeline dir, temp agent tree and its own HOME: seat addressing (cockpit descent, hyphenated seat dirs, @self), refusal of non-seat dirs / unknown agents / @boss, send-read-reply-thread roundtrip, attachments copied into the receiver's pad (and recorded in place when already there), a task that cannot be delivered filing nothing at all, and THE CHANNEL — the sender's session on the row with no receiver until one claims it, the stamp a woken run leaves, the reply binding to the session that asked rather than to its seat, the resume wake booked against that session's own workspace, delivery consuming the answer and cancelling the wake it beat, a runaway channel that stops waking anyone, and one timeline entry per seat at close.

subsystems.name: Inbox Stop Guard
subsystems.description: Serves both ends of a channel, once per (session, message) — blocks a session that owes an answer, and hands a session the answer it asked for. Binds only what is addressed to that exact session: the [inbox:N] its own first prompt was woken with, or a row bound to its session id.

test.description: Drives the real hook with synthetic Stop payloads: blocks the run woken for a task, never twice for the same item, never under stop_hook_active, leaves an unrelated headless worker and any other session in the seat untouched, hands the session that ASKED its answer and nobody else in that seat, consumes it by showing it, and allows on no-mail / non-agent cwd / kill switches / malformed input. Every switch is checked against a transcript proved to block without it.

subsystems.notes: Marker dir: {JSTACK_REVIEW_STATE}/inbox-guarded/<session_id>, holding the message ids already blocked on.

systems.notes: Self-contained python3 stdlib. Store is the `messages` table in {timeline_dir}/timeline.db — bin/msg is its only sanctioned writer, same law log_event holds for `entries`; the one crossing is at close, where an answered task writes one timeline entry per seat. An UPDATE is addressed to a seat and rides SessionStart injection. A TASK is addressed to a session: origin_session is the far end, bound_session is NULL until the spawned session claims it (naming one before it boots is a guess, in the column the whole anti-ambush rule reads), wake_job is the one-shot booked to carry it. A reply goes back to origin_session by whichever of two racing paths gets there first — that session's next Stop, or a fork-resume wake booked against the workspace it started in — so no liveness guess is needed anywhere. A task is NEVER typed into a session already running: a rung that did that (mail.deliver_live) was removed 2026-08-27 because mail addresses a seat and a seat is a chat dir, so every session it could resolve was a conversation, and it picked the most recently active one, which is by construction the one a person is typing in. A stop stays safe — it is the harness's own continuation channel and touches no composer. The scheduler rung is optional; with no `mail` config the inbox still files, injects and enforces, but a task cannot be delivered. Hosts adding entrances (share-sheet drops, dashboard forms) shell out to bin/msg rather than writing the table.
